findings.issue: The new string-aware scanner correctly closes R1 (all four rev-1 evasions now DETECT), but its full-line hash rule drops any src/http line that begins (after whitespace) with `#` — and in TypeScript a private CLASS-FIELD declaration/initializer line starts with exactly that. A field whose initializer reads the table, e.g. `class Handler { <newline>  #rows = q("select body from choros.agent_instruction"); <newline> }` is valid, shippable, compiling TypeScript (ES2022 private fields), yet the `  #rows = q(...)` line begins with `  #` and is dropped WHOLESALE by the strip, hiding the genuine table read. Live-reproduced on this exact branch against a real non-allowlisted file: appended that 3-line class to src/http/app-secret.ts and ran the gate → `SKIP FF-COMP-6: .../src/http/app-secret.ts — hit is comment-only ...` + overall `PASS: agent-instruction-runtime-dormant — all checks green` (exit 0). Independently traced through the scanner: the `#rows = q("...agent_instruction...")` line is emitted as EMPTY (`DROPPED->`), so the hit never reaches grep. Reverted via `git checkout -- src/http/app-secret.ts`. This is the SAME class of failure as R1 — a common, shippable code shape that hides a real code-level hit — and it directly contradicts the fix's own stated design rationale (script lines 60-65): the author kept MID-line `#` as code specifically 'never trade a new false negative for fewer false positives' to protect a private-field hit (`this.#agent_instruction`, pinned by probe R1-PRIVATE-FIELD, which DOES detect), but the DECLARATION form of that very case — `#field = ...` opening the line — is silently dropped. The full-line `#` rule serves no legitimate purpose in this scan: the gate only reads files under src/http (TypeScript/TSX), and TypeScript has no `#` line-comments, so the rule can only create false negatives, never remove a real comment.
findings.suggestion: Remove the full-line `#` special case entirely (line 79), or treat a line-leading `#` identically to a mid-line `#` (keep as code) — consistent with the author's own mid-line decision — since src/http is TS-only and TS has no hash comments. Add adversarial self-test probes pinning: a class private-field declaration line `  #x = q("...agent_instruction...")` MUST detect; and a field literally named `#agent_instruction` on its own line MUST detect. Re-verify AC-3 against these before re-granting the sanction.

findings.location: ci/checks/agent-instruction-runtime-dormant.sh:strip_comment_substrings() — inblock state carries to EOF with no reset
findings.issue: An unterminated `/*` (no closing `*/`) sets inblock=1 and consumes every subsequent line to EOF, so a real code hit below it is dropped and the file is SKIPped. Reproduced live: a clean file with `/* opened never closed` then `const rows = q("choros.agent_instruction");` → gate SKIP + overall PASS. NOT blocking because an unterminated block comment is a TypeScript syntax error (verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` on the fixture → `error TS1010: '*/' expected`), and `npm run build`/tsc runs earlier in the same npm run fitness chain, so such a file cannot ship — the read is not a shippable code-level hit. Flagged only as defense-in-depth hardening: the scanner's blindness beyond an unterminated comment relies on tsc as a compensating control rather than being self-contained.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking. Optionally, if inblock is still 1 at EOF, treat the file conservatively as a hit (err toward the gate reding, matching the module's stated 'always keep text' philosophy), or leave it to tsc. No action required for merge once R2 is fixed.
